answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy starts by pricing identity in work, not in weight. Before a fresh agent reaches the mesa where proposals are graded, it must collect attestations from established peers, each vouch earning the voter nothing but reputation risk. A wallet of relic tokens buys no shortcut, and a haven of cloned addresses cannot manufacture trust, because every admission raises the cost per fake. A swarm then pays more to exist than one honest participant, which is exactly the discouragement an open network needs.
